story_title: As Venue Staff, I want to mark a venue unavailable for a stated period and state when it will be available again so that it is only out of use for that period and comes back without me having to remember

acceptance_criteria.text: Venue Staff can mark a venue unavailable, stating the date and slot (AM, PM or Night) it becomes unavailable and the date and slot it becomes available again.
The date and slot it becomes available again must be later than the date and slot it becomes unavailable.

Given a venue is unavailable for a stated period, when a booking occupies a slot within that period, then it is flagged and the Coordinator notified as for a retired venue; bookings outside the period are not flagged.
Given the date and slot the venue becomes available again is reached, when that slot arrives, then the venue is available again from that slot without any action by Venue Staff.
Venue Staff can change the dates and slots of an unavailable period, or end it early.
Venue Staff must select the reason for an unavailable period (maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety, internal activity or other); when Other is selected, they must describe the reason.

open_questions: RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (Kristen, agreed with Kayal): the period is slot-level. Her Jira comment of 2026-10-04 had dropped slot-level periods; customer discussion #50 ('Can a venue be partially blocked? e.g. available mornings only during a renovation period' - answered with the three slots) is why they are back. The acceptance criteria in Jira were reworded on 2026-10-06. The story point estimate was not changed.

RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (Kayal): the screens and the story say 'unavailable', not 'retired'. That is the word the requirements and the other stories use: Week 7 Change #2 ('mark a venue temporarily unavailable'), Week 1 briefing ('Venue Unavailability Management'), Week 4 ('recorded periods of unavailability'), SPM-44, SPM-46, SPM-80 and SPM-87 ('unavailable period'), and the calendar already built ('Unavailable', 'Unavailable periods'). The BPMN (docs/ConnectSphere_BPMN.drawio, 'Venue retired, blocked or attributes changed') keeps retiring and blocking apart, as SPM-68 does ('venue retired, venue blocked'). The status lifecycle diagram covers event statuses only and says nothing about venues. Retiring stays SPM-39's separate action; a venue with an unavailable period stays Active and in the catalogue.

RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (Kayal): the reason picker is part of SPM-45 (AC6). The customer names the reasons a venue may be unavailable for (Week 1 briefing; Week 7 Change #2) but does not say a reason must be recorded - recording one is the team's reading, and Kayal chose to keep it. All 92 issues in the SPM project were checked and no other story covers it: SPM-55's reason is for equipment, and SPM-68 and SPM-87 only display what is recorded. Kristen's comment of 2026-10-04 had dropped it expecting a later story; none exists. Choosing 'Other' asks for a typed reason, which is required. 'Equipment failure' is a new stored value and the typed reason is kept in the period's existing notes column, so no schema change is needed.

RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (Kayal): the period is saved as a row in the existing unavailable-periods table (VenueUnavailability), not as new columns on the venue, so no schema change is needed. What reads that table was built by other stories - the calendar (SPM-46), venue search (SPM-40), and the booking request and approval checks (SPM-42, SPM-43, SPM-44). The calendar is used here to show what a period covers, and TC14 runs venue search once against a period, as the proof that the room is out of use for the period only; the booking request and approval refusals are not repeated (SPM-42-TC14, SPM-43-TC13).

RESOLVED 2026-10-06 (decided before the code, and built this way): a 'Mark unavailable' button on the venue page (S-20) opens a dialog titled 'Mark <venue> unavailable', rather than the separate Block venue screen (S-23) that UI_DESIGN.md sketches. Fields: 'Unavailable from' and 'Available again on' (dates), 'First unavailable slot' and 'First available slot' (AM, PM, Night), 'Reason' (required), and 'Other reason' (a text field shown, and required, only when the reason is Other; 500 characters at most). Messages: 'Enter the date the venue becomes unavailable.', 'Enter the date the venue becomes available again.', 'The venue must become available again after it becomes unavailable.', 'Choose a reason.', 'Describe the reason.' The period runs from the start of the first unavailable slot to the start of the first available slot, Singapore time (customer #36, #50).

RESOLVED 2026-10-06: wording chosen for the venue page - an 'Unavailable periods' section listing each period that is under way or still to come (not ones that have passed) as its reason, the typed reason when it is Other, and 'Unavailable from <date> <slot>. Available again from <date> <slot>.', with the buttons 'Change period' and 'End period'; message titles 'Unavailable period saved', 'Unavailable period changed' and 'Unavailable period ended'; the dialog 'Change unavailable period' with a 'Save period' button; the flag reads 'the venue is unavailable during this booking'. A venue may have more than one period (SPM-46 AC5 expects overlapping periods to exist).

RESOLVED 2026-10-06: a booking 'occupies a slot within that period' when the period covers any slot the booking holds, its setup and turnaround slots included (TC12) - the same rule the calendar's overlap warning and the booking conflict check use, and the one SPM-80 states for its own re-check. Only Approved bookings that have not finished are flagged (TC13), as in SPM-39.
